[[Medford, Oregon]] | tournaments = Y | tournament_list = * 4x ACC ([[2008 ACC Men's Basketball Tournament|2008]], [[2009 ACC Men's Basketball Tournament|2009]], [[2010 ACC Men's Basketball Tournament|2010]] & [[2011 ACC Men's Basketball Tournament|2011]]) * 4x NCAA ([[2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2008]], [[2009 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2009]], [[2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2010]] & [[2011 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2011]]) | championships = Y | championship_list = *2x [[ACC Men's Basketball Tournament]] ([[2009 ACC Men's Basketball Tournament|2009]] & [[2010 ACC Men's Basketball Tournament|2010]]) *2009 [[NIT Season Tip-Off]] *[[2009–10 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|2009–10 ACC Men's Basketball regular season]] *[[2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2010 NCAA Championship]] }} {{MedalTableTop}} {{MedalSport | Men’s [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|FIBA Americas U18 Championship]]}} {{MedalGold| [[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|2006 San Antonio]] | [[United States national basketball team|Team competition]]}} {{MedalBottom}} '''Kyle Edward Singler''' (born May 4, 1988){{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22727&SPID=1845&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=1211259&Q_SEASON=2007|title=Kyle Singler Bio|publisher=GoDuke.com|accessdate=October 29, 2007}} is a college basketball player for the [[Duke Blue Devils basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. He has been a four-year starter for the [[2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke men's basketball team]] and was instrumental in their 2010 NCAA Championship run, earning MOP of the Final Four. ==High school== Singler attended [[South Medford High School]] and was ranked as the fourth best college recruit in the nation from the class of 2007. In high school, he averaged 29.3 points per game and 10.6 rebounds per game as a senior.See [http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=1211259 GoDuke.com]. In 2007, Singler led South Medford to its first-ever state basketball championship, winning 58–54 over defending champion [[Lake Oswego High School|Lake Oswego]] and national standout [[Kevin Love (basketball)|Kevin Love]].{{cite news| last =Smith| first =Jeff| coauthors=Freeman, Joe|title =It's Panthers' turn| work =The Oregonian| date =March 11, 2007| url =http://www.oregonlive.com/prepboysbasketball/oregonian/index.ssf?/base/sports/1173599713127490.xml&coll=7| accessdate =March 11, 2007 }} A year earlier, Love and Lake Oswego had defeated Singler and South Medford for the state championship. Singler was a member of the Legends AAU team, along with former [[UCLA]] player Kevin Love, and participated in many prestigious all-American camps, including the Nike All-American Camp (Indianapolis), the Nike Peach Jam ([[Augusta, Georgia|Augusta]]), and the Main Event ([[Las Vegas, Nevada|Las Vegas]]). Singler was also named to the 2006 U18 USA Junior National team, alongside fellow top prospects [[Michael Beasley]], [[Jerryd Bayless]], and 2006 star recruit [[Spencer Hawes]]. Singler is also one of eight players featured in [[Gunnin' for That No. 1 Spot|Gunnin' for That #1 Spot]], a 2008 documentary directed by [[Adam Yauch]] of the [[Beastie Boys]] which was filmed in 2006. In October 2006, he signed a [[letter of intent]] to play college basketball at [[Duke Blue Devils basketball|Duke University]].{{cite news| last =Henry| first =Kris| title =Future looks bright for Singler, Blue Devils| work =Mail Tribune| date =October 28, 2006| url =http://www.mailtribune.com/archive/2006/1028/sport/stories/bk-nextkyle28.htm| accessdate =February 21, 2007 }} == College == '''2007–08 season''' As a freshman, Singler started at [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] and finished the 2007–08 season with averages of 13.3 points per game and 5.9 rebounds per game, helping lead Duke to a 28–6 record. Singler ended the 2009 season as the top scorer for Duke.[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/profile?playerId=36156 ESPN – Kyle Singler Stats, News, Photos – Duke Blue Devils] After Duke lost to [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]] in the second round of the 2008 [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]], Singler put to rest any speculation that he might enter the [[2008 NBA Draft]], saying:
I didn’t give the NBA any thought, I know I’m not ready. I need to mature both physically and mentally. I want to get stronger and quicker, and I want to work on learning how to play the game. I’m at a great place for that.{{cite news| last =Eggers| first =Kerry| title = Premature End Leaves Devil Blue| work =Portland Tribune| date =April 4, 2008| url =http://www.portlandtribune.com/sports/story.php?story_id=120725473519946700| accessdate =April 9, 2008}}
'''2008–09 season''' In January 2009, he had a career-high 16 rebounds against [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]], a game in which Duke won 76-67. '''2009–10 Season''' In February 2010, Singler scored a career-high 30 points against [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]], hitting a career-high 8 three-pointers in 10 attempts.{{cite web|url=http://goduke.statsgeek.com/basketball-m/players/career-highs.php?playerid=2472 |title=The Official On-Line Home Of Duke Statistics |publisher=GoDuke.StatsGeek.com |date= |accessdate=April 4, 2010}} In the ACC Tournament Final (playing Georgia Tech again), he hit a career-high 14 free throws. On March 28, 2010, in an [[Elite Eight]] NCAA game, as Duke beat [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] and advanced to the [[Final Four]], Singler (667 points), [[Jon Scheyer]] (690 points), and [[Nolan Smith]] (628 points) became just the second trio in Duke history to each score at least 600 points in the same season. In 2001–02, [[Jason Williams]], [[Carlos Boozer]], and [[Mike Dunleavy, Jr.]] first accomplished that feat for Duke.{{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22724&SPID=1845&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=204918040 |title=Notes: Duke 78, Baylor 71 – Duke University Blue Devils | Official Athletics Site |publisher=GoDuke.com |date= |accessdate=March 29, 2010}} Singler scored 19 points in the national championship game to reach 707 for the season, joining Scheyer (728) as the two became the second duo in Duke history to each score over 700 points in one season,{{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22724&SPID=1845&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=204923002 |title=Notes: Duke 61, Butler 59 – Duke University Blue Devils | Official Athletics Site |publisher=GoDuke.com |date=December 5, 2009 |accessdate=April 7, 2010}} following in the footsteps of [[Jay Williams (basketball)|Jason Williams]] (841) and [[Shane Battier]] (778), who did so for Duke's 2001 national championship team. Through the 2009–10 season, Singler was also 6th on Duke's all-time list in offensive rebounds (272), and 7th in defensive rebounds (490).{{cite web|url=http://goduke.statsgeek.com/basketball-m/players/misc.php?playerid=2472 |title=The Official On-Line Home Of Duke Statistics |publisher=GoDuke.StatsGeek.com |date=May 4, 1988 |accessdate=March 29, 2010}} For the season he averaged 17.7 points and 7.0 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/tournament/2010/columns/story?columnist=oneil_dana&id=5044890 |title=NCAA tournament: Duke Blue Devils' Lance Thomas and Kyle Singler pursue artistic side in the classroom – ESPN |publisher=Sports.espn.go.com |date=January 1, 2008 |accessdate=April 1, 2010}} He was 3rd in the ACC in 3-point field goal percentage (.399), 4th in scoring, 3-point field goals made (2.1 per game; his 8 against Georgia Tech were the most in the ACC in a single game for the season), and minutes (35.9 per game), and 7th in free throw percentage (.798).{{cite web|url=http://www.theacc.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2009-2010/confldrs.html#conf.wki |title=Atlantic Coast Conference Official Athletic Site – Men's Basketball |publisher=Theacc.com |date= |accessdate=April 3, 2010}} Singler was instrumental in Duke winning its fourth national championship, he was named NCAA Final Four Most Outstanding Player after averaging 20.0 points, 9.0 rebounds and 3.5 assists per game in wins over West Virginia and Butler. Scheyer called him "the toughest player I've ever played with."{{cite web|url=http://www.heraldsun.com/view/full_story/6713788/article-DuPree--Singler-earned-his-MVP?instance=most_popular |title=DuPree Singler earned his MVP |publisher=The Herald-Sun |date= |accessdate=April 2, 2010}} '''2010–11 Season''' Following the national championship, Singler considered entering the [[2010 NBA Draft]],{{cite web|last=Tysiacktysiac |first=Ken |url=http://www.charlotteobserver.com/2010/04/07/1361374/devils-should-have-talentto-make.html |title=Devils should have talentto make another NCAA run |publisher=CharlotteObserver.com |date= |accessdate=April 7, 2010}} but ultimately decided to return for his senior season at Duke.{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/news/story?id=5115934|title=Singler to return to national champs|date=April 19, 2010|accessdate=April 20, 2010|publisher=ESPN.com}} Singler was named the pre-season [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] player of the year, pre-season first team All-ACC, and was named a pre-season first team All-American. On November 27, 2010 Singler tied his career high 30 points against his brother E.J. Singler and the [[Oregon Ducks]]. Singler was also voted to the Atlantic Coast Conference first team. For the 2010-2011 season, Kyle Singler, is averaging 17.1 points, 6.9 rebounds, and 1.6 assists in 35.0 minutes per game for the Blue Devils. The Blue Devils were eliminated in the Sweet 16 in the tournament against the [[Arizona Wildcats]] by the score of 93-77. Singler had 18 points in the defeat.http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310830150 ==Personal life== Singler's parents were both athletes at [[Oregon State University]]: his father, Ed Singler, was quarterback of the football team, and his mother, Kris Brosterhous, was on the basketball team. Four of Singler's uncles played [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] football, baseball or basketball. His younger brother, [[E.J. Singler]], plays basketball for the [[University of Oregon]].{{cite web|author=E.J.
